about: A person's level and its stat points (docs/design/skills-v2.md §12.1-12.2 as the owner's order 88 changed it, D-178, D-181; src/people/9999975-level). The level IS the power ladder's level (data/power.json levelCurve): one scale. A person is seeded at the level the ladder computes from his fighting worth, and from then rises only by defeating people and beasts, read on the same ladder, plus a floor for growing up. Experience is kept as the share of the way to the next level (0 to 1).

xp.about: Experience is counted in defeats of a man of one's own level (a peer), from the level gap alone, so a rescale of the ladder's might cannot move what a life earns (orders 91-93, D-184). Rising from level L to L+1 asks need(L) = e0 x growth^L peers (each level 1% more, so the gaps widen: orders 87, 89) x wall, where wall is 1 except on the step into a hundredth level (99 to 100, 199 to 200 ...): wall.mul[k-1] for the k-th wall, the last number for every wall after. One defeat of a foe of level F gives 2^((F - L) / upHalf) for a stronger foe (past upTo, upTo x the root of the rest) and 2^((F - L) / downHalf) for a weaker one: every foe gives something, whatever his level, a weaker one far less (no line any more). Calibrated (the README; the owner's anchors of orders 93 and 94): from 30, soldiers (130) give about 94 after 20 defeats, 116 after 50, 128 after 80 and thin out far below 200 (158 after 1,000: against men of 130, a level at 160 asks some forty of them); knights from 200 against knights (265) about 214, 238, 265 after 20, 80, 300, and 281 after 1,000, while one who beats the best (320) breaks through 300 (329 after 1,000); the elite cross 300 and 400. The walls are thresholds, hard but crossable, never ceilings (order 94): each asks six to fifteen times the step before it, so a life thins out as the cost climbs and the able break through.

foes.about: Foes with no sheet of their own: a man killed in a battle or on a mission (a regular soldier on the owner's anchors of order 93, 80-180) and anyone else killed (an average grown person, 20-50).

floor.about: Growing up: a person stands at least at floor(age) = grown x (age / the race's grown age)^pow, where grown = 24 + (mean potential - 42) / 3, held to 20..30 (the owner's average human 20-30). After the grown age only defeats raise the level.

points.about: Each level brings points (a race may set its own with GD.RACES[r].points), and one more at every bonusEvery-th level. A stat's ceiling is the person's potential x capMul (as A.train's); the body's room at an age is the ceiling x (roomChild + (1 - roomChild) x age / grown) below the grown age, the whole ceiling after; old age, wounds and illness lower what is read, not what is placed. A point costs 1 below half the ceiling, 2 to three quarters, 3 above. Placed points never move.

ways.about: The ways of life a household's or a post's placement leans to: two stats and who lives so. A career key of GD.CAREERS, or a post read from the person's offices, rank and occupation.
